previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with a history of CAD s/p CABG, COPD, GERD, chronic esophagitis, and alcohol abuse was admitted after experiencing severe epigastric and chest pain following a large greasy meal and alcohol consumption. He described the pain as sharp and pressure-like, worse than typical heartburn, prompting him to call for help. Initial evaluation included cardiac monitoring, negative troponins x3, and an EKG showing no acute changes, ruling out myocardial infarction. Imaging revealed gastric dilatation with no evidence of pneumonia or heart failure. Pain improved with morphine, antacids, and nitroglycerin. He was managed for alcohol intoxication with IV fluids, thiamine, and folate, and monitored for withdrawal without complications. Due to baseline dysphagia and aspiration risk, he was kept NPO initially and evaluated by speech therapy before advancing to soft diet. His acidosis resolved with hydration, and anemia was attributed to hemodilution. By discharge, he was pain-free, tolerating oral intake, and stable vitally. He was discharged home with services, new ranitidine prescription, and follow-up plans for substance abuse counseling and primary care.

___ yo male with history of CAD s/p CABG, HL, h/o CVA, HTN, COPD 
who presents with bradycardia accompanied by his baseline 
lightheadedness.

#. Bradycardia: He presented with bradycardia incidentally 
noticed on a visit from his physical therapist.  He denied any 
new symptoms accompanying his bradycardia, although did continue 
to have persistent dizziness that he describes more like 
vertigo.  Worsening of his vertigo while an inpatient was not 
related to low heart rates on telemetry and his bradycardia was 
not considered to be symptomatic.  He has had bradycardia in the 
past with documented heart rates in the upper 40's and 50's.  
Other causes of bradycardia were also evaluated and he was ruled 
out for MI and his thyroid function was within normal range.  
His medications were reviewed for possible causes of bradycardia 
but no changes were made.  

#. CAD: Patient is s/p CABG in ___, with no complaints of chest 
pain although does endorse shortness of breath on exertion.  He 
was continued on aspirin, Plavix, atorvastatin and smoking 
cessation was encouraged.

#. Alcohol abuse: He has a history of significant alcohol use in 
the past, but currently has not had a drink for >1 month.  He 
was continued on acamprosate and oxazepam per recent psychiatry 
notes, although the patient did note that he had not reliably 
been taking his acamprosate as an outpatient.  He was also 
continued on thiamine and folic acid.

#. COPD: He has SOB on exertion at baseline.  He was continued 
on his outpatient inhalers, although he states he rarely uses 
them at home.

#. Hypothyroidism: He has recently had his dose of levothyroxine 
increased and was euthyroid based on lab studies during this 
hospitalization.

#. Anemia: Continued outpatient iron

#. DVT prophylaxis: He received SC Heparin for DVT prophylaxis 
during this stay

#. Code Status: Patient was FULL CODE during this 
hospitalization
